questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding forms of government:
A. An alliance formed by political parties after elections when no party secures a clear majority is called a coalition government.
B. Appropriation refers to setting aside money for a specific purpose, prorogation is the termination of a House session by the President, and allegiance is a tie that binds an individual to an institution or person.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct definitions of the respective political and parliamentary terms used in the Indian context.

questions.question: The period between prorogation of Parliament and re-assembly in a new session is called______.
questions.solution: While adjournment is a short break within a session, the long interval between the end of one session (prorogation) and the start of another is called a recess.

questions.question: In the absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha, who presides over the joint sitting of the two houses of Parliament?
questions.option_2: Any senior member of Rajya Sabha
questions.option_4: Any senior member of Lok Sabha
questions.solution: If the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are unavailable, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides. Note: The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President) never presides over a joint sitting.

questions.question: The salary and allowances of leaders of opposition in parliament are governed by the Act passed for the first time by the parliament in the year ______.
questions.solution: Statutory recognition and official salary/allowances for the Leader of the Opposition were established by an Act of Parliament in 1977.

questions.question: The Vice-President of India is part of which branch of the government?
questions.solution:
The Vice-President of India holds a dual role in the Indian governance system:
  • Executive: As the second-highest constitutional authority in the country.
  • Legislative: As the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

questions.question: Which body is responsible for resolving disputes related to the election of the President of India?
questions.solution: According to Article 71 of the Indian Constitution, all doubts and disputes regarding the election of the President or Vice-President are settled by the Supreme Court. Its decision is final. Notably, under Article 71(2), even if an election is declared void later, the acts performed by the President before that decision remain valid.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in relation to the enforcement of President's Rule?
questions.option_1: The Governor's recommendation can lead to dismissal of a State government, even if it enjoys a majority.
questions.option_2: It can be extended indefinitely with the consent of the Prime Minister.
questions.option_3: The President cannot impose President's Rule unless the Supreme Court permits.
questions.option_4: President's Rule can be declared without Parliament's approval.
questions.solution: President’s Rule is imposed under Article 356 when a state government cannot function according to the Constitution. While intended for constitutional breakdowns, it has historically been used (and sometimes misused) based on a Governor's report to dismiss state governments, even those holding a majority, as highlighted in the famous S.R. Bommai case (1994).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a condition for the President’s office in India?
questions.option_1: He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence
questions.option_2: He shall not be a member of either House of the Parliament.
questions.option_3: The allowances shall not be diminished during his term of office.
questions.option_4: He shall not hold any office of profit.
questions.solution: Article 59 outlines the conditions for the President's office. Specifically, Article 59(3) states that the President is entitled to use his official residences (Rashtrapati Bhavan) without payment of rent. Therefore, option (a) provides a false condition.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India expressly provides that the President is eligible for re-election?
questions.solution:
Article 57 explicitly states that a person who holds, or who has held, office as President shall be eligible for re-election to that office. For context:
  • Article 54: Election of President
  • Article 56: Term of office
  • Article 58: Qualifications

questions.question: In the state legislative assembly, the Money bill can be introduced with the prior permission of __________.
questions.solution: Similar to the President's role at the Union level, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly on the recommendation of the Governor. This is part of the special procedures for financial legislation under the Constitution.

questions.question: As per article 123, the ordinance making power is the most important legislative power of ____________.
questions.solution: Article 123 grants the President the power to promulgate ordinances when either House of Parliament is not in session. These ordinances have the same force as an Act of Parliament but must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of its reassembly.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that ‘there shall be a Vice President of India’?
questions.solution: Article 63 simply mandates the existence of the office by stating, "There shall be a Vice-President of India." Article 64 further establishes that the Vice-President will serve as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: The ________ of every state unfurls the flag in its capital on the Republic Day.
questions.solution: On Republic Day, the Governor (the constitutional head) unfurls the flag at the state capital. In contrast, the Chief Minister performs the flag hoisting ceremony on Independence Day.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles states that the Prime Minister should be appointed by the President?
questions.solution: Article 75 deals with provisions for Ministers. It states that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President and other ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most controversial Article in the Indian Constitution, which provides for President’s rule in any state?
questions.solution:
Article 356 is often called the most controversial because it allows the Union to take control of a State's administration. Other related articles include:
  • Art. 352: National Emergency
  • Art. 360: Financial Emergency

questions.question: Who is considered the highest law officer of the state in India?
questions.solution: The Advocate General (Article 165) is the highest law officer of a State. The Attorney General is the highest law officer for the Union. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor and holds office during their pleasure.

questions.question: Which Article deals with the election of the President?
questions.solution: Article 54 specifies that the President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.

questions.question: As per article 158, the Governor shall NOT be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in ___________ Schedule.
questions.solution: Under Article 158, if a person who is a member of Parliament or a State Legislature (under the First Schedule) is appointed Governor, they are deemed to have vacated their seat in that House upon entering the office of Governor.

questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President?
questions.solution: Part V (The Union) of the Constitution covers Articles 52 to 151, including the office and election of the Vice President (Article 66).

questions.question: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution: Gulzarilal Nanda served as the Acting Prime Minister twice (after the deaths of Nehru and Shastri), each time for only 13 days. While Atal Bihari Vajpayee also had a 13-day stint in 1996, Nanda's total combined tenure in acting roles remains the shortest distinct service periods.

questions.question: In case the President is satisfied with the Governor’s report, he may declare President’s Rule under Article 356 but such proclamation is initially for a period of ________.
questions.solution: A proclamation of President's Rule is valid for six months once approved by Parliament. It must be approved by both Houses within two months of its issuance. It can be extended every six months up to a maximum of three years.

questions.question: Among the following, which is not a qualification for membership in the Vidhan Sabha?
questions.option_1: Not hold any office of profit
questions.option_2: Have attained the age of 25 Years
questions.solution: While practical knowledge is helpful, the Constitution does not list "Knowledge of Politics" as a legal requirement. The mandatory qualifications are being a Citizen of India, being at least 25 years old, and not holding an office of profit.

questions.question: The minimum strength of the Council of Ministers in a state as per the Indian Constitution is ________.
questions.solution: As per the 91st Amendment (2003), the total number of ministers (including the CM) in a State must not exceed 15% of the Assembly strength, but it shall not be less than 12.

questions.question: Who has the power to prorogue the House or either House of State Legislature from time to time?
questions.solution: Under Article 174, the Governor has the authority to summon the House, prorogue (end a session) either House, and dissolve the Legislative Assembly.

questions.question: Which option is NOT correct in case of appointment of a Governor?
questions.option_2: Cannot hold any office of profit during his tenure
questions.solution: The standard tenure for a Governor is five years, not six. However, they serve at the pleasure of the President, meaning they can be removed even before the 5-year term ends.
